html:
Mirza Fatali Akhundov was a writer and thinker, born in 1812 in Shaki in northern Azerbaijan, who wrote the first plays in Azerbaijani Turkish and is seen as the founder of modern Azerbaijani literature.

He worked as a translator for the Russian viceroy in Tiflis. Between 1850 and 1855 he wrote six comedies mocking superstition, greedy officials and ignorance, which were staged across the region. He argued for replacing the Arabic alphabet with a simpler one, an idea that was realised in Azerbaijan only in the 1920s. His Letters of Kamal ul-Dowleh attacked religious authority and royal despotism in Iran. He influenced reformers in Iran and the Ottoman lands and the Jadid movement among Muslims of the Russian Empire.
